alerts.title: Progressive creatinine rise and eGFR decline on TDF-containing ART
alerts.message: Guidelines advise monitoring creatinine/eGFR on TDF, and creatinine should be checked even at non-routine times when renal function may deteriorate. Patient has been on TDF/3TC/DTG for 3 years. Creatinine has risen steadily from 0.9 mg/dL (2020) to 1.4 mg/dL (2026), with eGFR now 52 mL/min/1.73m2 and new urinalysis proteinuria 1+ and glucosuria trace. This trend is clinically significant even though the latest value alone may appear modest. Ibuprofen 400mg taken 2-3 times weekly for 6 months is a plausible contributor to nephrotoxicity alongside TDF, and dehydration or intercurrent illness should be excluded. Unexplained fatigue may reflect renal impairment.

evidence.recommended_action: Repeat creatinine/eGFR and urinalysis promptly, assess volume status, and review TDF use with renal monitoring; discontinue or stop NSAID (ibuprofen) use. Consider switching TDF to a less nephrotoxic NRTI per guidelines if renal decline is confirmed.

alerts.title: Viral load monitoring interval on DTG-based ART
alerts.message: Guidelines recommend viral load every 6 months on DTG-based first-line ART, reducible to 12-monthly only after VL <50 copies/mL for over 1 year with reliable adherence. The patient's latest viral load is <50 copies/mL with adherence >95%, so the current 6-monthly review schedule is consistent with guidance; no monitoring gap identified for viral load, but the plan should explicitly document the next VL date.

evidence.recommended_action: Document next viral load due date (6 months) and whether the 12-monthly interval is appropriate once sustained suppression over 1 year is confirmed.
